series: What does Islam say about promises, covenants and pledges
rules: Every Quran ayah: Arabic + 7 translations fetched live from api.alquran.cloud per the standing sourcing rule; never from memory.
Every hadith: Arabic + English verified live (sunnah.com page and/or hadith-api); zh/ko/ja/ms/th/es are own translations labelled on-slide as such, unless a real edition exists.
One ayah or hadith (or one tight consecutive pair) per post so wording stays exact and clear in every language; mark progress in 'done'.

Candidate lists were produced by keyword search of the live Quran (en.sahih: promise/covenant/pledge/oath) and of the full English Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Dawud, Tirmidhi, Nasai, Ibn Majah, Malik and Nawawi collections on 2026-10-13. Coverage is the major explicit texts; no claim that it is every narration in existence.

hadith.topic: three signs of a hypocrite incl. breaking a promise

hadith.ref: Bukhari 3178 / Muslim 59 (fawaz 210) / Abu Dawud 4688 / Nasai 5020 / Tirmidhi 2632
hadith.topic: four traits: lies, breaks promise, treacherous covenant, evil quarrel
do not make a promise only to not fulfil it
intended to fulfil but unable: no sin
great treachery: lying to a brother who trusts you
banner for every treacherous person on the Day of Resurrection
killing one under a covenant: not smelling Paradise
the Prophet: I do not break a covenant
Umar: fulfil Allah's covenant with those under protection
end of times: promises broken, trusts betrayed
pledge to an Imam kept only for worldly gain
none more truthful in fulfilling promises (Abu Dharr)
Talhah, one who fulfilled his covenant
Badr: O Allah I ask You to fulfil Your covenant and promise
violating a covenant with a Muslim: curse of Allah and angels
